CHAPTER III

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 8

1. Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of domestic violence, protection of women's rights in employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of human trafficking.
2. Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.
3. Protection of women's rights in employment rights domestically or abroad receive protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.
4. Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.
5. Protection of women's rights from acts of human trafficking includes prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts of human trafficking.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya. 2. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Tasikmalaya. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency area. 6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 12. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 25. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction in order to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA is a technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children who experience problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems; 31.

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 44

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 34 letter c is a service provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who need continuous handling.
3. Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
4. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus that have the main duties and functions in implementing affairs of:
a. social;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
5. In addition to being implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation can also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

Article 32

1. The community as referred to in Article 29 letter c is obliged and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER XIII

SANCTIONS

Article 64

1. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatuses that have the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Sub-District Level Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children, Village Level Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 33

1. Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 29 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and report if violence occurs and protect victims.
2. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members which shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Paragraph 6

Protection of Child Victims of Physical and/or Mental Violence and Children with Disabilities

Article 31

1. The village government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to the village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the medium-term village development plan.

Part Six

Child Protection in the Social Field

Article 26

3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

1. Regent is the Regent of Tasikmalaya. 2. Regency Area is the Regency Area of Tasikmalaya. 3. Regency Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of regional government administration. 5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Regency area. 6. Women's Empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental, spiritual, social capacity, knowledge, and skills so that women are ready to be utilized according to their respective abilities. 7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation. 8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 12. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 25. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Article 42

1. Legal aid services as referred to in Article 38 letter a number 4 are to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.
2. Legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully explain the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

CHAPTER XI

MONITORING, EVALUATION, AND REPORTING

Article 60

Monitoring shall be conducted periodically and in an integrated manner every 6 (six) months by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection in coordination with Regional Apparatuses or other units that handle women's empowerment and child protection.

Article 44

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 34 letter c is a service provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who need continuous handling.
3. Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
4. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus that have the main duties and functions in implementing affairs of:
a. social;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
5. In addition to being implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation can also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

CHAPTER XIII

SANCTIONS

Article 64

1. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatuses that have the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Sub-District Level Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children, Village Level Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 55

1. The Village Level Children's Forum as referred to in Article 52 paragraph (2) letter c is a forum for children's participation in the Village area whose members consist of representatives from Neighborhood Associations and Community Associations of at least 1 (one) girl and 1 (one) boy.
2. The Village Level Children's Forum is established by Village Head's Decree with a term of office of 2 (two) years.
3. The Village Government as the Supervisor of the Village Level Children's Forum facilitates the formation of the Village Level Children's Forum starting from the selection stage, validation of management and guidance in capacity building of members of the Village Level Children's Forum.
4. Community institutions existing in the Village have the obligation to accommodate and foster children's participation in development and in advocating for children's rights.

1. The community as referred to in Article 29 letter c is obliged and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER III

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 8

2. Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.
3. Protection of women's rights in employment rights domestically or abroad receive protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.
4. Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.

Article 64

2. Regency Regional Apparatuses that have the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Sub-District Level Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children, Village Level Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 33

1. Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 29 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and report if violence occurs and protect victims.
2. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members which shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 31

1. The village government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to the village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the medium-term village development plan.

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 32

1. The community as referred to in Article 29 letter c is obliged and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 31

1. The village government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to the village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the medium-term village development plan.

CHAPTER III

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 8

1. Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of domestic violence, protection of women's rights in employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of human trafficking.
2. Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.
3. Protection of women's rights in employment rights domestically or abroad receive protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.
4. Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.
5. Protection of women's rights from acts of human trafficking includes prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts of human trafficking.

Article 41

Health services as referred to in Article 38 letter a number 3 include:
a. first aid to victims by competent officers;
b. treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical and paramedical personnel; and
c. referral to health services as needed.

Article 42

1. Legal aid services as referred to in Article 38 letter a number 4 are to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.
2. Legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully explain the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER II

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 2

1. The Regional Government has the obligation and responsibility for the implementation of women's empowerment.
2. Women's empowerment efforts as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. determination of policies, budgets, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.

Article 44

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 34 letter c is a service provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who need continuous handling.
3. Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.

a. social;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.

Article 9

1. The Regional Government is obliged to provide protection to women in order to realize and enjoy a decent standard of living.
2. Provisions regarding Protection as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 42

1. Legal aid services as referred to in Article 38 letter a number 4 are to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process.
2. Legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by:
a. providing legal consultation that includes information regarding the rights of victims and the judicial process;
b. accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and helping victims to fully explain the violence they experienced; and
c. coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Article 31

1. The village government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to the village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the medium-term village development plan.

SANCTIONS

Article 64

1. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.

c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Funding for women's empowerment and child protection shall be sourced from:
a. regional revenue and expenditure budget;
b. village revenue and expenditure budget; and
c. other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 25. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction in order to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA is a technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children who experience problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems; 31.

CHAPTER XIII

SANCTIONS

Article 64

1. Any person who intentionally violates the provisions of Article 10 or fails to provide protection against forms of violence against women and children as referred to in Article 25 and Article 26, and fails to provide the rights of women and children as referred to in Article 27 and Article 28, thereby causing violence to occur, allowing violence to occur, and/or failing to report and failing to provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in laws and regulations.
2. Regency Regional Apparatuses that have the duties and functions of administering women's empowerment and child protection that fail to carry out their obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
3. Management of P2TP2A, Sub-District Level Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children, Village Level Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within the internal institutions or respective organizations.

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER III

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 8

1. Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of domestic violence, protection of women's rights in employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of human trafficking.
2. Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.
3. Protection of women's rights in employment rights domestically or abroad receive protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.
4. Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.
5. Protection of women's rights from acts of human trafficking includes prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts of human trafficking.

Article 7

The implementation of women's empowerment in the legal field as referred to in Article 3 letter d includes:
a. improvement of knowledge and awareness in the legal field through communication, information and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and consultation services as well as free legal aid.

Article 31

1. The village government as referred to in Article 29 letter b, is obliged and responsible to:
a. formulate and implement programs and activities related to the protection of women and children;
b. implement the protection of women and children from violence;
c. realize a Child-Friendly village; and
d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence according to the village financial capacity in each fiscal year.
2. In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the village government formulates programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the medium-term village development plan.

Article 33

1. Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 29 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and report if violence occurs and protect victims.
2. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members which shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 46

UPTD PPPA as referred to in Article 45 letter a is a technical implementing unit to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children who experience problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems.

Article 44

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 34 letter c is a service provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who need continuous handling.
3. Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
4. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus that have the main duties and functions in implementing affairs of:
a. social;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
5. In addition to being implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation can also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

Article 34

The Regional Government implements activities for the implementation of protection of women and protection of children, which include:
a. prevention;
b. services; and
c. social rehabilitation.

CHAPTER III

WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Article 8

1. Women have the right to obtain protection from acts of domestic violence, protection of women's rights in employment, protection of women in emergency situations and special conditions as well as protection of women's rights from criminal acts of human trafficking.
2. Protection of women's rights from acts of domestic violence in the form of prevention of physical and psychological violence, sexual violence and neglect, handling, services and empowerment of victims of domestic violence.
3. Protection of women's rights in employment rights domestically or abroad receive protection in the prevention and handling of cases of neglect of women's rights in terms of employment.
4. Protection of women's rights in emergency conditions and special conditions, includes protection of women in emergency situations, in conflict areas, disaster areas, protection of the rights of women with disabilities, and protection of the rights of elderly women with social problems.
5. Protection of women's rights from acts of human trafficking includes prevention and handling, services and empowerment of victims of criminal acts of human trafficking.

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 32

1. The community as referred to in Article 29 letter c is obliged and responsible for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
2. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include:a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 33

1. Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 29 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and report if violence occurs and protect victims.
2. In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may be transferred to the Regional Government and other family members which shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 32

b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
4. Neglect as referred to in Article 25 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after children as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/orc. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 9. Women's Protection is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 10.
