Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully. 12. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 13. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child. 14. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 15. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household. 16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 17. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises custody as a Parent over a Child. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations. 20. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service. 21. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs in the Tasikmalaya Regency area. 22. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanism of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect. 23. Handling is an action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect. 24. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 25. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred. 26. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative of an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence. 27. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction in order to carry out social functions properly. 29. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 30. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for Women and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPPA is a technical implementer to carry out operational technical activities in its working area in providing services for women and children who experience problems of violence, discrimination, special protection and other problems; 31.

Article 26

1. Physical violence as referred to in Article 25 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
2. Psychological violence as referred to in Article 25 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering to women and/or children.
3. Sexual violence as referred to in Article 25 letter c, includes:
a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1\. physical harassment;
2\. verbal harassment;
3\. gestural harassment;
4\. written or pictorial harassment; and
5\. psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

a. acts that result in the failure to fulfill the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

5. Exploitation as referred to in Article 25 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
6. Other violence as referred to in Article 25 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
7. Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
8. Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person or victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 44

1. Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 34 letter c is a service provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
2. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who need continuous handling.
3. Special social rehabilitation for women victims of domestic violence and trafficking in persons is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
4. Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus that have the main duties and functions in implementing affairs of:
a. social;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
5. In addition to being implemented by Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation can also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.
